title: global variable
body:
A variable outside every function, visible to all of them and alive for the whole run of the
program. [[Variable Scope]] and [[Variable Lifetime]] in first year own the language side of
this; the reason it turns up here is different.

**A global is the shared state that creates the [[Critical Section Problem]].**
[[Thread|Threads]] of one process share the address space, so they share every global. Two
threads incrementing the same global is the canonical race, and it is why
[[Synchronization]] exists.

It is also how the mechanisms are built: the `lock` in [[TAS]] is a shared global int
initialised to 0, [[Peterson's Solution]]'s `flag[]` and `turn` are globals, and a
[[Semaphores|semaphore]] is a global counter. The tool for guarding shared globals is
itself a shared global; what makes it safe is that it is only ever touched by atomic
operations.
